Caller ID, texts, email and incoming calls notifications are a higher intensity vibration than others I've tried. I have always felt the Mi Band 3 vibration regardless of what I'm doing. I really like this while my phone is muted so I remember to check it later. I can also read the shorter messages if my phone is out of reach.

I can't vouch for degree of waterproofing but it's certainly shower and dish washing proof which is good since the Xiaomi Mi Band is lightweight and very comfortable so I often forget I'm wearing it.

I like that I can set it when I go to the gym and get a reading on steps, distance, heart rate, etc. This becomes a subset of the daily activity record.

The sedentary reminder is helpful when I'm ‘in the zone’ while working on a project. I'm not convinced the heart rate is accurate but I suspect it's fairly close for those if us not needing a medical reason to monitor our heart. I don't believe much of anything the Sleep Monitor says but then I don't care about that either.

The battery life is at least 2 weeks. I've only charged mine 3 times in 2 months.

Nothing is perfect, including this Mi Band 3. Navigating through the myriad of settings can be frustrating. There is definitely a learning curve when trying to figure out how to see a specific option : Swipe up? Swipe down? Swipe to the side? Which side?

The other issue is when it changes to military time or suddenly jumps an hour or two ahead/behind for no reason. It took me awhile to find the fix for these problems. Shut down Bluetooth and turn off phone for a minute or two. Turn phone back on, turn on Bluetooth and after about a minute everything should go back to the way you had it originally. I've only had each of these problems happen once.

I am very impressed with the Mi Band 3. And the options can't be beat, especially for the price. This would be a good starter fitness band for a kid or someone just wanting to see if a fitness band is useful to have.
text_fidelity_b: Xiaomi Fitness Tracker, Mi Band 3 Heart Rate Monitor Activity Tracker Watch 50M Waterproof Smart Bracelet 0.78 OLED Display Weather Forecast Wristband Pedometer Calories Burned Sleep Monitor Black

Cutter 66384 Camping-Candles, pack of 1, silver If you take the time to research the product, regardless of who markets it, you will find that citronella, as a mosquito repellent, does not, will not, CAN NOT do what it is advertised to do.
The best mosquito repellent is a slight breeze. These insects have extreme difficulty flying/navigating in the slightest breeze.

The reason you see dead mosquitoes in the wax, flame (or light of most types) attracts them. When they fly into the flame, wings, antennaeI, and proboscis get burned off. They fall into the hot wax, and die.

I buy these, locally, to use while fishing. Buy only for the light provided.
To sum it up: people have been told, for decades, that citronella repels mosquitoes, they are persuaded that it works, not noticing a slight breeze, in stead it’s, “Oh, my word! This stuff works!!!”
Do some research. Read a bit. And save your money.

text_fidelity_a:
Withings Pulse Wireless Activity Tracker + Sleep and Heart Rate Monitoring, Black UPDATE 1/17/2015

I had this for a year, and loved using it -- until it stopped working. I had purchased 6 of these in total (5 as gifts), and at least 2/6 of these things no longer hold a charge. When I emailed support, because I contacted them just over the year mark (Jan 6th purchase date), the best they could offer me was a 25% discount. It's great when it works, but such a high failure rate within a year seems disappointing.

==========================
The Withings Pulse claims to track your activity, your sleep, and your heart rate.

If you're looking for something that is precise and accurate for exactly what you've done, this isn't it. I don't think the technology is quite there yet in any device.

But if you're looking for something that is effective as a motivator, and that gives you a consistent baseline to measure your progress, this is perfect for that.

I've been eyeing activity trackers for some time. Many of my friends choose the Fitbit while others chose the Nike Fuel band. I finally pulled the trigger on this device specifically for a few reasons:

1. Integration with a smart scale. I think if you're really motivated to change yourself - get more active, lose some weight, you want to get the smart scale with it to close the loop. It is that much more rewarding and encouraging to keep up with your daily goal if you see the results of your work (whether it's lower fat %, lower weight). The Fitbit also has a scale, but I liked that the Withings scale had been around for longer. Sure you could just get any scale and put in manual measures to your app, but I'm a lazy person and having all of that integrated and automatically synchronized is a big deal.

2. Works for both iPhone and Android. I can't find the studies right now, but it's far easier to get fit and stay healthy if everyone else is doing it too. So for group motivation and support, when I finally committed to the Withings platform, I went ALL in and got 6 trackers + the Withings scale as Christmas presents to myself and everyone around me. The fact that it works on both mobile platforms is a big plus. As was getting a group of us on this at the same time. Our friendly competition has definitely pushed me on the days I felt like slacking off.

3. Accurate enough. When I've gone on hikes and walks with friends who run, we've ended up with roughly the same number +/1 100 steps (albeit different calorie counts) at the end of the trail. So while it might not exactly match the listed distance on a trail you've gone in terms of miles, it is at least consistent enough with itself which is the most important thing. Also, while it might log a few steps as I'm moving the pulse from the strap to my pocket and vice versa, it consistently does that so I'm going to know on any given day if I've done net more or less.

4. Has motivated me. I wasn't sure how well this thing would work, but the simple act of having a concrete measure of my activity has motivated me to move and do more than any other system I'd set up for myself before. I periodically glance at my tracker during the day, and find myself adjusting (ok an extra-long route to the store, maybe stepping in place while I'm on the phone, pacing while I watch TV). Knowing exactly how much I've done means there's no excuse for me to "feel like I've done a lot". I know if I've been active. Or not.

5. Good customer service. I'd read online that people have had problems with their customer service. My personal experience was far from that. 5 days after I got the tracker, my clip holder broke. Personally I think it's poorly designed as the repeated act of taking the clip in and out of the holder every night to move put in your night armband for sleep tracking is going to add a lot of strain to the corner of the clip. Well I emailed customer service and they offered to replace my clip for free. I just sent them my proof of purchase and 9 days later a package arrived from France. I can't believe they sent the replacement from France but I'm happy to have the replacement.

6. Detailed app and web interface. I haven't seen the competitor apps, but for me, the web site and the app contain all the information I need. At a glance, I can see my overall trends (compared to the normal range), and I can see my weekly trends of when I'm sleeping, how well I'm sleeping, when I'm most active. I tried integrating MyFitnessPal. I couldn't stick with that kind of dedicating food logging, but if you're that kind of person, the integration gives you a complete in/out/impact picture.

7. Decent battery life. I'd say your tracker will last well over a week with regular use. And it charges back up quickly (maybe 15 minutes). The first days I got my tracker I was religiously syncing my tracker with my phone several times a day a few days later I'd only used about a bar of battery.

That said the device does have some limitations:

1. The plastic clip is really fragile. I've read reviews of people having problems with the clip falling out of the holder. To be safe, I keep the pulse in my pocket. At $99 (or $70 during the Christmas sale), I sure don't want to be dropping and losing this thing that often.

2. Some sort of data override would be nice. Given that the sleep tracker works by being strapped to your body, the assessment of light and deep sleep (or being awake) is measured by your amount of movement. I can be prone to insomnia, but sometimes that involves just lying awake and feeling frustrated. It usually doesn't involve thrashing around like a mad person because I'm so upset I'm awake. So the tracker has mistakenly taken my lack of motion to mean I'm in blissful deep sleep. I wish! It'd be nice in those cases to add manual entries (the way you can with weight) to add notes. But in generally there is a correlation where more deep sleep (or sleep overall) has resulted in feeling more rested the next day.

Bottom line: The results

How are the results? This was a gift to myself for Christmas. Since then, I've used the tracker every day and have committed to doing 10,000 steps every day. I didn't change my diet and still continued to eat a few pieces of chocolate and some kind of dessert once a day. This is not to say I prescribe this as the best way to get healthy. I just happen to have a healthy love of food and was also curious to see what straight up physical activity would do to my weight. I've never been overweight and lead a relatively active lifestyle, but 8 months of living off mayonnaise laden hotdogs while living in Chile did leave me a little plumper than I cared to stay

So 19 days into this I've walked an average of 73K steps every week and slept an average of close to 8 hours. I have gone from 111 lbs to a trendline average of 108 lb (naturally my weight will fluctuate at every measure but it steadily goes down.). I feel great and am feeling as motivated as I was on day one. Short of accidentally washing this thing or losing it, I'm going to keep using the Pulse and keep tracking! This device has been one of my favourite purchases in recent memory.
text_fidelity_b: Withings Pulse Wireless Activity Tracker + Sleep and Heart Rate Monitoring, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Igloo Thermoelectric Iceless 28-40 Qt Electric Plug-in 12V Coolers This served me well for three weeks on the road. The items you put in this need to start out cold and you need to buy a separate wall adapter for hotel rooms. I bought a cheap one from Coolbuy that worked well. This cooler does seem to keep the temperature cool when left in the car overnight though. This is easy to clean because the motor is on the top.

One issue I had is that after a couple weeks I noticed standing water on the bottom which soaked some items I had. I am not sure if that was from condensation or if a bottle leaked a bit. It would be good if this came with a small removable platform to keep items off the very bottom in case condensation starts to puddle.

The lid is heavy and can pinch your hand if it slams shut.

The cord placement is not ideal because it blocks some of the handle movement when plugged in. This is an issue because the handle needs to be in a certain position for the top to open fully.

Update. I have used this on more trips and have concluded that the condensation is from the cooler. The cooling fins ice over and then melt when the temperature rises high enough. I routinely see pools of water on the right side that soak anything underneath. This cooler is a damp cool, not a dry cool like a regular freezer. This is problematic for anything made of paper or cardboard in the cooler. I am lowering my rating to three stars.

My fix was to use plastic risers that came with some stay-fresh plastic containers meant to hold vegetables. It adds about one centimeter of space between the cooler contents and the bottom where the water pools.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo Thermoelectric Iceless 28-40 Qt Electric Plug-in 12V Coolers

Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software I have used a few different Omron pedometers in my day and like other consumers, I purchased this one due to the solid reviews. Anything with an overall rating as good as this product should be worth the money. So, with my old pedometer on the fritz, I decided it was time for a new one and purchased this model.

Omron Pocket Pedometer was okay at first. It does measure your total steps, aerobic steps, time, calories burned, and distance. The accuracy seems to be pretty good and I like that I can monitor my progress and check things online with the software. These are all good qualities and they earn the product some respectability.

Where this product loses some points with me is with its cumbersome display; its tendency to go blank; and the lack of any ability to shut it off. With the display, what I don’t like specifically is the annoyance with looking at your statistics from past days. It stores up to a week’s worth of data, which is great, but if you want to view the data from a past day, you have to toggle back and forth between two of the buttons. You can’t just simply go back to the day you want and then view the steps, aerobic steps, time, distance, and calories with one push. You have to push the button to the left a couple of times, then push the button on the right to view one stat, then push the button on the left a couple of times again to view the next stat, etc. Other pedometers are much easier than this.
Another problem is with the tendency of the screen to go blank. This happens to me anytime I drop the pedometer. I have to then get a small screwdriver to remove the back, move the battery around, and screw it back on. The display will them reappear. And, of course, there is the problem with inability to shut the pedometer off. With other pedometers, you can turn it off or it will shut off itself after a certain amount of time has elapsed. It doesn’t work that way here. The display is always on, draining the battery at a fast rate. Sure, you could pop out the battery after each use, but this is too much trouble. Just make sure you have plenty of replacement batteries on hand because you’re going to need them.

So, taken as a whole, this is device is not as good as I expected and I plan to search for a replacement very soon. It’s disappointing for something from Omron. I have had better luck with other pedometers from this company and cannot give this one a recommendation for the reasons cited.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software

text_fidelity_a:
JACO MBX-60 Presta Tire Pressure Gauge for Bikes (Max 60 PSI) | MTB & XC Series The old saying that a person who has one watch always knows what time it is, but a person who has two watches is never sure, comes to mind here. If this is your only pressure gauge and you dial in your tire pressures based on this tool, you’ll be happy. But if you have a couple of different gauges like me, some on pumps and another that is independent like this one, then you won’t be exactly sure which one is accurate.

However, consistency and precision is what matters. Based on several years of use and comparison to two other gauges and my car readouts, I trust my digital gauge on my bike floor pump for accuracy from psi ranges in the mid teens to the mid 50s. I took readings from several different pressures as benchmarked with my pump, and this analog gauge consistently read about 1 psi lower. That consistency is more than good enough for me. And by way of background, I’ve set up my mountain bike and gravel bike with tubeless tires, and I am particular about the pressures I run in different conditions.

Also, this gauge has a rubberized face and comes in a sturdy and well padded case. Since this is a precision instrument, I appreciate the protection to keep this device working well.

Overall this is an easy to use tool that feels like it will last a long time (as long as you don’t abuse it).
text_fidelity_b: JACO MBX-60 Presta Tire Pressure Gauge for Bikes (Max 60 PSI) | MTB & XC Series

The second scooter came in COMPLETELY different packaging. We shall see if it can stand the test of time. I did get the insurance as based off many reviews, this thing is not going to make it long, so I did want to be covered.

You are getting what you pay for here. DO NOT step on the rear fender and I would also not recommend folding, as it snaps onto and stresses the fragile rear (plastic) fender. They also structurally tied the rear foot breaking mechanism into the rear fender as well. Cannot stress enough how not strong and flimsy this rear fender situation is. However for whatever reason, it is an integral part of the functional design of the scooter in many ways. If it snapps off, you are done with the rear foot break.

However for the price, still throwing up 3 stars. Cant expect the world at this price point.

The zippers are not going to take much use, in fact the whole thing might be good for one season of regular camping and use/abuse.

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Spot Headlamp My favorite low priced headlamp.
Not the quality of high tech wonder lamps. But there are no real faults. And the interface is very good.
All inputs on one button which is the best way to do it, fewer moving parts to go wrong.
3 inputs : momentary push, 3 second push, 6 second push.
If the lamp is on :
Momentary push cycles on/off.
Long push gradually dims the light in steps.
(when it reaches the dimmest it will flicker once to indicate lowest level,
then it gradually brightens the light, step at a time, flickers once on highest).
This works very well to set the brightness levels.

When light is OFF:
momentary push turns it on (two outer lights for flood, or center for spot. Repeat pushes will alternate: spot, off, flood, off, spot,...
3 second push : turns on the red lamp
6 second push: turns on the lock mode (locks lamp off until another 6 sec. push turns it back on. A blue light on the side will go on for a couple seconds to verify the lamp is locked).

I find the interface easy to use to get it to do as I like when I like.
5 different tilt settings from straight down to higher than straight forward. There are settings I find perfect for reading or watching your step on the trail. And they stay put.

Very bright on spot!
The flood is very spread out, lights up the whole room or tent.

5 stars.
------

Another lamp that costs about $10 more is the Princeton Tec EOS TACTICAL. The tactical model of the EOS line is military issue from several governments. Bulletproof and rugged, really waterproof. But the ergonomics are military rough: the button is very hard to push (so it won't wear out), the battery box takes a tool like a dime to open (so they could never fall out by mistake). A better choice if you going to climb mount Everest and your life depends on the lamp. Not as good as this BDSH for using in common outdoor camping, running, hunting, imo.

Those are the two under $50 that I like.

EDIT: I should have noted the reviews stating the tilt lock stops would fail. They failed in 6 months on one of mine of these. The other two I have are getting weaker and weaker (about a year old). Then the lamp just tilts all the way forward and points at your toes. No way to reset the tilt after the mechanism breaks. I changed my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars. I do NOT recommend these.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Spot Headlamp

When you’re ready to use it, preparation couldn’t be easier. You simply unfold, unroll and shake it out a few times. Using the corner air valve you inflate the pad. The innovative design requires little effort or air to completely inflate.

I’ve used, tested and reviewed several different similar products and what makes this product unique is the honeycomb air pocket cells. While this pad is not very thick I found it was really comfortable.

When finished using it, deflation is equally straightforward. You’ll release the air - I found it easiest to open the valve and completely roll the pad starting at the end opposite of the valve. Once I had the air expelled, I folded it back like it was originally and tightly rolled it back up then slid it back into the nylon sack.

This is a high quality product that is easy to inflate / deflate and is compact for storing and carrying when you’ll use it.

This is definitely a product I’d recommend.

Streamlight 69300 TLR-1 Series and & TLR-2 Glock Style Contour Remote, Black ORIGINAL REVIEW: This DOES fit a G21 Gen4 setup. When I got the package it states that it won't fit the TLR-2G. My goodness, why couldn't this info be shared during the product description here or the manufacturers website? I really needed this to work because my TLR-2G doesn't stay activated after a few rounds of fire with the regular cumbersome reach and toggle switch.

UPDATE 07/28/14: After having to sell my TLR-2G, I picked up the standard red-laser TLR-2HL. The directions are a little lacking but I was able to figure it out. Fit is very tight, but that is how you want it so the switch doesn't fly off during use.

TIPS: The push pin for the original battery door will need to be removed. If you are looking into the battery compartment, you will be pushing the RIGHT end of the pin towards the left. Once you have about an 1/8 inch of exposed pin, you will need to use some needle-nosed pliers to pull it out the rest of the way. Save the pin for later use just in case.

Here is where the included directions are a little lacking. The thin metal 1/4 inch wide clamp that held the original door down is NOT to be removed. You will be using that same clamp to clamp down the new hinge-less remote. It took me a few minutes to realize this. I was getting ready to take the clamp completely off via another push pin. I'm glad I didn't. Now, loosen the rail clamp on the light as wide as you can, trust me on this. Insert the trigger end first, then the light's rail clamp to your Glock's rail.

Single press and it lights up. Double tap and you get strobe. At least that what seemed to be working for me.

Like another reviewer shared, ff you have big hands, yes, you will notice that your fingers are slightly off natural position. This is a trade-off I'm willing to make so that I am not toggling with the original switch with my off hand. I am not a LEO, this is strictly for home defense use. I'd rather keep my off hand supporting my shooting hand or holding an extra mag if needed.
text_fidelity_b: Streamlight 69300 TLR-1 Series and & TLR-2 Glock Style Contour Remote, Black

MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking UPADATED AGAIN: I have purchased both the 1 and 2 person tent. Seems like very well quality and lightweight. However, the ONE thing that is bad about BOTH tents is the way the end tie outs are sewn and sealed. The tents BOTH leak at the tie out points. This is due to the way they are sealed. It seams as if the seam seal was applied FIRST and then the tie outs sewn into the fabric. This allows water to come through the stitching and leak into the tent. POOR DESIGN. I have remedied this by using seam sealant on ALL stitch points for the tie outs. So, word of caution for everyone owning and buying these tents. MAKE SURE YOU SEAM SEAL EVERY TIE OUT POINT. Once you do that, this tent should be waterproof.

UPDATE: I set this tent up in my yard to test it for waterproof and durability. We had a rain event that came through. No heavy storms. Just light to medium rain that only lasted 10 or 15 minutes. The tent leaked at both ends where the tie outs are sewn into the fabric. These points are seam sealed, so I do not know why or how it leaked at both points. The water on the floor of the tent was about the size of a quarter.
I have since sprayed all of the fly seams and the tie out points with silicone treatment. When we get another rain storm coming through, I will set it up again for another test to see if the spray will keep the tie out points from leaking.
Also, both sides and the rear of the fly, down at the edge, collect water and allow it to pool up. This is a design flaw. I had the tent as tight as I could get it, without damaging the material. The water pooled up around the bottom edge looked like a small moat, and could lead to large amounts of water to run under the tent. This could soak through the floor and get your sleeping gear wet.
I fixed this issue with some micro tarp clamps and 550 cord. I attached one at each end, and two in the rear, one on each side between the rear stake out point and each corner. So 4 total. When I set the tent up again for another rain test, I will update with pictures.
So far, this tent was NOT the tent that all the hype was about. The ONLY positive thing so far, is that it is a true double wall tent, and that will keep condensation out of the sleeping area.

I have not used this tent yet, only set it up. However, with just having set it up, I can see that I will probably like this tent. But, one thing I would like to have seen with it, is more fabric at the vestibule. When set up by the directions, the edge of the vestibule is quite high off of the ground. This would allow for good ventilation during a summer night, but in a rain storm, I would be afraid of rain being blown in.
I have it set up in the yard, and we have a chance of rain today/tonight, so once I let it get rained on and take it out on a trip, I will update my review.
text_fidelity_b: MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking

text_fidelity_a:
Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire I purchased Campy Shamal 2-way rims a couple years back. I then purchased everything needed to mount and maintain tubeless tires including Fusion 3s. I ride a '12 Specialized S-Works Roubaix and mostly do fast training rides about 3 to 4 days a week with longer rides beyond 60 miles fairly regularly. I weigh out at roughly 185 pounds.

Tubeless and ceramic bearings are somewhat in the same category these days in terms of bikers wondering if this equipment truly makes a difference. Well, I've ridden ceramic bearings in my crank and in my wheels...and YES...it makes a difference...now...I've ridden on tubeless for two riding seasons...and YES...they make a difference. Tubeless is the future...as it is in nearly every vehicle that has wheels from a riding mower to a motorcycle to a car...and mountain bikes. Why it has taken so long with road biking is understandable...change is hard...and manufacturers will go where the money is.

First, let me make this clear...putting the Fusion 3 tires on was a chore...and I mean...a CHORE. It will test your patience. Do NOT succumb to using levers as it will ruin the bead. Google tubeless tire installation for help but even then it will baffle you as to how you're going to get that tire over the rim...but...you will...and the benefits will be worth it.

Second, it takes a few rides to get the tires truly seated. Use an air compressed pump if you've got it...but...I had a "Joe Blow" floor pump that worked fine. I didn't install the sealant until after the second short ride and pump up. You will most likely lose quite a bit of air at first but as the tire seals over time...the air pressure stabilized. I do pump up my tires before every ride but it isn't out of the norm of my former clincher tires.

Third, I've ridden my fusion 3s at 90psi on the front tire and 100psi on the back. The ride is fast & super smooth. A lot of riders think super high psi is better but that is, (arguably for some), not true because at a high psi your tire is actually bumping up and down off the road which drains energy transfer over time. The benefit of running tubeless at lower psi is that the tire remains in more constant contact with the road which...over time...equals better energy transfer...and hence...speed, comfort, and endurance. Also, there is some evidence that without a tube you eliminate friction...I'm honestly not sure about that claim...even so, I can say from experience that I'm not going back to tubed tires...tubeless tires run as advertised.

Fourth, durability...I run typical roads here in Maryland over countless miles...up and down hills...less maintained side roads...and these Fusion 3s can go yet another season. The wear is normal with no unusual issues. I've NOT had one flat tire. I've NOT added more sealant since the first install...which I should've done...but...it hasn't made a difference.

Fifth, the only reservation I have is getting a flat tire but I guess it's a good thing that I'm not as use to dealing with flats like I had for my tubed tires. I have to say it has been a pleasure to not have had one flat for two seasons.

I'd like to try the ATOM version of this tire...and I think I'll get it just for comparison purposes. Not looking forward to the install and my expectation is that they will not fit my riding style, endurance expectations, and my higher weight...even so, I'm a believer in trying anything once...so...we'll see.

All in all...educate yourself but don't be afraid to go tubeless. It is change that we all seem to avoid but I'll never go back now that I've tried it out...and as the biking money goes...tubeless quality and selection will as well. ENJOY!
text_fidelity_b: Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire

text_fidelity_a:
TETON Sports Celsius XXL Sleeping Bag; Great for Family Camping; Free Compression Sack After decades of backpacking with mummy sleeping bags, and never having enough warmth, we transitioned to 4WD tent camping. Although I never really minded the confines of a mummy bag my wife was never crazy about it so we looked for a bag with lots of space, width, and warmth. Weight and bag compression was no longer the primary criteria for purchasing a sleeping bag. That's good because this baby is relatively heavy and doesn't exactly pack small once taken out of the box, but that's fine for 4WD camping.

Experience has taught me that you want to purchase a sleeping bag that is rated at least 20 to 30 degrees colder than the coldest temperatures you expect to encounter. We occasionally camp in the mountains where night time temps drop into the high 20's and low 30's, but most of the time the night time temps are in the 40s to low 70s in a relatively dry Western-US environment, including the high desert. I was concerned we might overheat but my wife and I have remained comfortable across the entire temperature range wearing just a t-shirt and underwear or long underwear. She zips her bag up completely whenever the temps drop into the 40s or lower. I don't think I've zipped mine up completely yet.

We're no longer sleeping on a thin foam pad on the ground. We use these bags on cots with 3" thick foam pads. We both sleep like a rock. Our mummy bags have been handed down to our grown kids. As sleeping bags go, this one is a winner!
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports Celsius XXL Sleeping Bag; Great for Family Camping; Free Compression Sack

text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Stash Rack Bike Floor Stand Bicycle Storage Organizer This is a simple and easy to assembly bike rack. It works perfect for us.

it took me all of 15 minutes to put together for 3 bikes. I love that you have the option to expand it to 5 bikes if needed. (more on that later). The instructions were easy to follow (I've included a pic).

What's in the box: This comes with everything you need to assemble your frame, even a little hex wrench which is the only tool you need other than your two hands. All the pieces are nicely packed in the box and have plastic over them to protect them from getting scuffed up in the box. Your box should have 2 frame tube ends, 10 frame tubes, 10 wheel arms, 5 wheel arm binders, 20 hex-head screws, and one hex wrench.

Assembly: The bottom bars for the frame pretty much snap together with little push in metal buttons to hold them in place (see pic). The holes for the buttons are nice and oblong so you have room to twist/maneuver them when attaching the wheel arms to get the holes aligned when screwing them in. The only slight issue I had is the hex screw heads. A few of them seemed to easily strip when I was doing the last few turns with the provided hex wrench. I was not even tightening them very tight so there was not a lot of torque. I figured they were probably just cheap screws, but they still did the job fine. The screws you can twist by hand easily once you get the holes aligned correctly then just use the hex wrench to finish up. Once you have the wheel arms attached the wheel arm binders easily attach at the top of the wheel arms but squeezing them together slightly then just slide the binder down next to the frame once it is on. And that's all there is to it!

using the stand: we have 3 bikes - 2 mountain bikes and 1 road bike. I thought I may have to add a spacer to the frame since the mountain bike handle bars will not fit if the two of them are right next to each other in this stand. I did try putting one in backward, with the rear wheel in the stand, but the bike stand arms were too narrow for wheel and derailer to completely fit into the stand. however, my road bike is small enough that it fits just under the mountain bike handle bars. putting that in the middle solved the issue! Now we have all three bikes neatly parked in a corner of the garage rather than leaning against the wall and boxes. yay! And if we happen to acquire more bikes, we can always expand it.

Overall this is a decent, simple bike stand that does what we need.
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Stash Rack Bike Floor Stand Bicycle Storage Organizer

text_fidelity_a:
M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch Extreme Graphite Fly Fishing Rod 4-Piece 9 Feet with IM7 Carbon Blank, Hard Chromed Guides, A Cork Grip（Size:3/4/5/6/7/8/10wt） (Extreme Rod, 9ft 4weight) Let's just say it. This is a darn nice rod. Is it a Sage? A Reddington? A Loop? Of course not. But it's also not $400.

I got this rod because I have 5wt and 6wt rods which were a bit more costly, but I wanted a 4wt for some smaller streams I'm going to be hitting. I won't spend much time there, and money is not abundant, so I figured I would try one of these. Boy was I surprised! I was expecting some moderate (slow) action rod, sloppy, and Heavy. This is light, crisp, and a joy to cast! The cork is great for this price point, and it's all put together and presented quite nicely.
There's an attitude in fly fishing that if it's not expensive, it's not worth using. Unfortunately we don't all have the ability or desire to spend $500 on a rod. For those of us in that situation, this is a magnificent option.

Look at it like this. You buy a rod at Scheels or Cabela's because you're getting a quality product at a slightly discounted price because it's store brand rather than big name brand. And that usually is the case and works well. Some of the best fishing gear I've got, and I've got a lot, was got from those brands I just named. These Maxcatch rods are built on the EXACT same blanks that the Scheel's Outfitter MDD fly rods are built on. And those were being sold for $100.

With that in mind, know that when you get one of these you aren't getting a Loomis rod. But this is probably the best sub-$120 fly rod you can get, and that leaves a lot of money for flies, tippet, line, and a reel.

I'll update this review with pics next time I go out. Buy one of these with confidence. I'll probably buy another for my wife and get a 3wt for me. I'm sold on this brand!
text_fidelity_b: M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch Extreme Graphite Fly Fishing Rod 4-Piece 9 Feet with IM7 Carbon Blank, Hard Chromed Guides, A Cork Grip（Size:3/4/5/6/7/8/10wt） (Extreme Rod, 9ft 4weight)

text_fidelity_a:
Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

I bought this based on it conforming to the face and being Therapeutic. However, I often sleep with my head raised up or in my recliner because of breathing issues due to my sinuses.The silk of this pillow would always cause it to slip down or sideways causing me to wake up and recenter it on my eyes. Overall, I would recommend this pillow for someone who doesn't have to sleep with the head or upper body raised at any height and doesn't have to turn their head much while napping. The silk does have a cooling effect and the lavender and chamomile does help to relieve some of the pressure and pain.
text_fidelity_b: Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow

text_fidelity_a:
CyclingDeal Folding Bike Foldable Bicycle with 7 Speed Shimano Gears 20-inch Aluminium Wheels Easy Folding City Bicycle with Disc Brake, Rear Carry Rack, Front and Rear Fenders I have several folding bikes for use by the family. We swear by them.

Our first folding bike was a Euromini Campo. I bought one, then we purchased one for my wife. Those bikes were a nice low-end introduction to folding bikes with a $200 price point. About a year later I purchased a Dahon Vigor. An excellent bike at a $750 price point. An order of magnitude superior to the Euromini bikes in terms of many components and build and ride quality (one Euromini frame has a crack near the seatpost and we had to replace both bottom brackets after only a year).

This CyclingDeal bike, although a brand unknown to me, provides a level of quality on par with my Dahon Vigor. In terms of features, the CyclingDeal comes with superior brakes (disc), equivalent quality tires/rims and several features the Vigor lacks (fenders, quality rear rack). Other components such as headset, bars and grips are of significantly lower quality. The CyclingDeal shifting, while inferior to the SRAM system of the Dahon, is equivalent to the Euromini Campo, consisting of a 7 Speed Shimano with Revoshifter. The Aluminum frame is MUCH lighter and somewhat stiffer than the Campo and ride quality is closer to that of the Dahon. This is also the lightest adult folding bike I've ever used. About 2 lbs heavier than my son's folding Vilano cuiser (we added a longer seat post, brakes and a sprung saddle). If you have a Campo, you'll notice how much lighter the CyclingDeal is...

If this bike said Dahon on the side, no one would bat an eye. From a distance. A closer inspection of the frame shows a slightly lower weld quality/frame construction as well as low-end consumer detailing ("super easy folding system...")

If you're looking for a first folding bike on Amazon. This should definitely be in the running. You will only need to replace the bar grips with some Ergon GP1s. And maybe the saddle if you weigh more than 200 lbs.

To like: quick release wheels, disc brakes, lightweight frame, fenders, rear rack
To hate: low-end detailing, cheap grips, no magnetic closures on folding system

Recommended!

I'll update this review after 100 miles...
text_fidelity_b: CyclingDeal Folding Bike Foldable Bicycle with 7 Speed Shimano Gears 20-inch Aluminium Wheels Easy Folding City Bicycle with Disc Brake, Rear Carry Rack, Front and Rear Fenders

text_fidelity_a:
Energizer Vision HD Performance Metal Flashight Lots of confusion on the reviews concerning this product mostly because two very different models were submitted to reviewers. This review is for the smaller 250 lumen model that takes three AAA batteries. It is short (about 3.75"), sturdy, and comes with three AAA batteries and a lanyard. The case is attractive with an industrial look but probably too smooth as far as texture for some people to work with. And yes, the package was relatively difficult to open, probably to discourage five-fingered shoppers from stealing them off the shelves. Unfortunately there are no instructions included for those who may not intuitively figure out how to install the batteries and use the three lighting functions (high, low, strobe).

Being short, slippery, and not confidence inspiring as far as using it -- and only having an estimated 2.5 hour battery life -- what is this really good for? The functionality is in its small size and very bright light. This would be an excellent tool for those working in small and dark spaces, casting enough clear and bright light for close detail work. Working under a sink with a Maglite LED 3D Cell Flashlight just doesn't cut it. This Energizer is small enough to prop up against anything in your work area to help focus the beam while freeing both hands for whatever task you're undertaking. The light beam cast by it broadens quickly and the choice of a "high" and "low" setting increase its usefulness. Believe it or not, it can actually be too bright for close work using the "high" beam.

This 250 Lumen Energizer is fine for short operating periods either inside or outside the house. However its very limited battery life restricts it to use as a back-up flashlight. For overall effectiveness as an emergency light source (blackouts, storms, indoor/outdoor security) nothing really beats a Maglite LED Flashlight using 3 D batteries. For $22.72 (compared to $14.99 for this Energizer) you have a 168 lumen light which casts a beam as far as 412 meters and has an eight hour battery life. We have several in our home that are red in color which makes them easier to find in a stressful situation. Not only that, but the Maglites are hefty enough to use as a striking weapon if need be. It's certainly better to have in your hand than nothing at all.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer Vision HD Performance Metal Flashight

text_fidelity_a:
AppFinity - AppFishing I used to own a Radica Bass Fishin' game, until the reel on the device broke. No, I wasn't violent with it. Actually, I think it broke because I sat on it (I was a heavy child). Nevertheless, I had much fun with it, and wanted a replacement ever since.
When I saw this available for the iPhone, I snatched it right away, hoping to relive the Radica days.

I noticed right away that the menu is a little confusing to navigate. The app developers chose to go with a heavy app--meaning graphically and operationally--which sucks battery and requires lots of interactivity to work it properly. Once I got fishing, though, it was pretty simple.
And that's another problem; it's *too* simple. I get a bite as soon as I drop the line, which sort of diminishes the fun. Reeling in fish is trickier, with a lot of the line cutting almost always. The reel could also use some sensitivity adjustments, because my slowing down didn't reflect in the app itself.

I think the main complaints I have are with the app itself, so we could see major improvement in the future.

The device itself is great and sturdy. It held the iPhone safely and seems like it'll last a long while.
text_fidelity_b: AppFinity - AppFishing

text_fidelity_a:
WILD MAN Bike Bag, Bike Accessories, Bike Phone Holder Bike Phone Mount, Waterproof Bike Phone Bag, Mountain Bike Accessories for Adult Bikes with 3D Hard EVA, TPU Touch Screen and Sun Visor for Phones Under 6.7" This is a sort of gem in a way considering I have never heard of the brand. The quality is fantastic to the point where you could easily mistake this for an expensive, established brand. AND...even though Wild Man is or is not a good name, at least it makes sense, more or less, for a bike accessory.

Anyway, it seems like they got everything right, but just be advised that this is NOT the type of case where you can see your phone through the top, despite saying it's compatible with all these devices; that's just a way to add search terms, and I guess it's technically correct that those phones will fit in this bag.

While I haven't had this out in a downpour, it has what appear to be excellent quality, self-sealing zippers on the exterior that should be essentially waterproof as far as rain goes (likely not submersible). It's sort of a "shell" case in that it is semi-rigid, and the material has a checkered carbon fiber look to it, which is neat looking and will likely match a lot of fancier bikes, but will work with anything since it's basically black.

The three straps come large enough that I imagine they can be used with any bike, and can be adjusted down as necessary; I expect the cleanest and nicest installations will involve trimming the excess. The one strap is "across" the opening of the two sections, which would limit how far you can open it, except there is a piece of fabric inside artificially limiting how far you can open it, perhaps so that the former's limitation is not so obvious, but I suspect it will help keep you from dropping stuff out of the case while it is installed on the bike.

One side is a half-height net, and the other side is a full height zippered net, both of which offer some stretch, and are very much like a good piece of luggage.

This definitely adds a little bulk to your bike, and I'm not convinced everyone will want on for permanent storage (there are lots of other placement options to consider), but I can imagine that this goes quite far when doing multi-day riding with camping stops. The great thing is that it can be taken off and put back on quite easily, and as needed.
text_fidelity_b: WILD MAN Bike Bag, Bike Accessories, Bike Phone Holder Bike Phone Mount, Waterproof Bike Phone Bag, Mountain Bike Accessories for Adult Bikes with 3D Hard EVA, TPU Touch Screen and Sun Visor for Phones Under 6.7"

adidas Essential Combo Training Bench with weight Set, 100 lb Physical strength training is a good idea. Some people join health clubs and use their machines to provide the training they need, but one good and economical alternative is to have a weight bench of your own. And this is where the Adidas Essential Combo Training Bench with Weight Set can help. It has everything you need to begin meeting your fitness goals.

Adidas training bench is a useful, although basic weight bench. You get the bench plus a leg lift and a set of weights that total 100 pounds. It’s nice to get an all in one set because you don’t need to shop separately for a set of weights when you purchase the bench. You can use this for bench press and leg lifts, which makes it just right for beginners.

The weights included with this set are vinyl in construction, so nothing fancy but they are sufficient for the task. I like the easy to remove and tighten clamps on the barbell- you don’t need any special tools to put them on or take them off. This is better than the weight sets of the past, many of which required a wrench to fasten and loosen the clamps. The bench is good too- nothing amazing, but rather very utilitarian and capable of helping you build strength.

Weight sets are a good addition to any home. They will easily pay for themselves over time, when compared to joining your local gym. This set is basic, but it accomplishes what it promises and even though it won’t meet the needs of more advanced weight trainers, it has enough going for it to meet the needs of beginners and enough quality of design and construction to recommend.

I'm a bit different than most folks because I actually sleep on a 20" tall queen size air mattress every night and have done so for the past two years.  The thing is, with the air mattress I can move and sleep in may different positions and my body feels supported.  That's not exactly how or why I use a pillow.  Again, I'm not like most people - I have been sleeping with a 100% down pillow for so many years I can't even remember when I bought my first one.  I mention this because of the way I use a pillow when sleeping - it is molded, puffed out and reformed several times during the night.  That just can't happen with this air pillow. It does store well in the very small case it comes in and that's perfect!  As I have gotten older and had to move when I didn't really want to but circumstances made me, I have become addicted to "nomadic furniture" that is easier to move than traditional furniture.  An air pillow does fit within my parameters of small and packable!  Same with my bed - not quite a small, but certainly nothing like lugging around a heavy, floppy queen size mattress and box springs!  So, all in all, I am pleased with this air pillow at least for what I will use it for.

text_fidelity_a:
Stack-On PS-1520 Gun Safe I've had my safe for a couple weeks now and I am pretty happy with it. I was looking for an inexpensive safe to keep valuables away from the casual thief. This safe is not going to stop a professional thief. For that type of safe you need to pay upwards of $500. This safe is also not fire or waterproof so if you need those types of features look elsewhere.

The safe weighs about 40 pounds so it is critical to bolt it down, otherwise a thief can just walk off with it. There are 4 holes in the back of the safe and 4 holes in the bottom. There were 4 pretty hefty screws provided, I mounted my safe inside a large cabinet and it seems pretty secure. The safe and door are made of pretty heavy gauge steel so it is not going to be easy to just pry it open.

Inside the safe there are two metal shelves held in place by cheap plastic fasteners. But I will get into that later. Programming the security code was very easy and I had no problem opening and closing the safe. The safe also comes with two keys in case you forget your code or if the batteries die. There is a pretty loud beep when the buttons are pressed but that can be turned off.

I just have two minor issues with the safe. First, the cheap plastic fasteners used to hold the shelves in place are useless. When I opened the safe they were laying in the bottom of the safe with the shelves and half of them were broken. Easily resolved though, I just used metal bolts and screws I had to hold the shelves in place. I think manufacturer should provide these. The second issue I had was with the cheap shelf liners provided. They are very thin foam material and don't stay in place when sliding things in and out. Again though easily resolved by replacing with more substantial liner.

Overall I am pretty happy with this safe. I looked at others in the price range and many seemed to have significant quality issues. The issues I have with this safe are very minor and to be expected for a safe at this price point. This safe is a good value for your money as long as you are just looking to protect valuables from a casual thief
text_fidelity_b: Stack-On PS-1520 Gun Safe

Stansport Polar Shield Emergency Tent Super long (90+ inches long) and durable, basically as expected and required. While it could be used more than once, it is really one of those things that are a one and done sort of thing (it will never fold back down small). It is the typical long tube. Of course, how much room you have left over depends on your body size. I have never had one rip. Good for short term shelter and warmth.

I am a big fan of the tents. I always keep one in my every day carry, and my hiking bag. While I do keep emergency blankets on hand, I actually prefer these tents over the flat blankets as it can be used as a sleeping bag. or can be cut and shared.

Cheap enough worth while addition to any pack, emergency kit, car kit, etc. I love stuff like this and often replenish, and often buy stuff like this as gifts.

I dont rate on price, but I do comment. Current price of $8.33 is a little more than I normally spend on the tents, but not entirely unreasonable. It is perfectly fine quality, and will do the job as needed. Some kits come with extra goodies, but I cant attest to the quality.

text_fidelity_a:
Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs I’ll be honest, I’d never heard about exercise plate machines until I saw this one. I looked it up and according to the articles I was reading, this is an under used exercise machine type and actually does help loose weight. So I decided to grab this LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine and try it. I come away surprised, but happy - it does help me. My wife and I have been active in living a healthier lifestyle and approach with a variety of activities, from kickboxing and walking to weights to... well, this thing. My wife is still sidelined from her severely broken foot, so she has not tried it yet, but I have and I’m blown away by how it works.

The machine arrives in a box that is easy to remove from - all the parts are fit correctly and easy to get out. It is slightly heavy - nothing one can’t move, but it has some weight to it. I’m not sure the actual size, but we can’t fit it under our bed, so we’re still working on where to keep it - but that’s not an issue. There are instructions - I would suggest also doing a little research. I learned a few things from articles I was reading. There are also resistance bands and for your arms resistance ropes as well. The instructions are well done and offer ideas for working out as well.

The unit has a remote so you don’t have to get off or bend down to alter things. I have used it every time - I will increase or decrease the various options while still on it. This comes in handy for severity of the vibration as it is intense and I’ll inch it up or down during the workout. I have not gone very high - I want to say around 15 - and appreciate being able to try things or adjust as I need.

ONE CON: The power cord is short. I have to use it primarily in our bedroom where my wife is currently working from bed, so that limits when I can use it. If it were at least another 2 - 3 feet long it would be perfect. I’m going to move some things around and try to make it work in the living room, but if not... anyways, if they changed that this would be a perfect unit.

I really love the workout. It is... (not) easy. I mean you’re standing on this vibrating plate and you do feel it. The level, the time, going up and down, the truth is, your body works to stay there. I’ve only stood on it and done planks, and both were workouts. I got off sweating. I’ll say, standing on it is less of a vibration to my head than the plank - I can’t go as long or as high at a single time because in the plank position I feel like my head will vibrate off. But I can feel my core working.

I like this unit so much that when I saw a foot massager from the same company I grabbed it. While you can use this as a foot vibrator, I thought to help my wife heal - when cleared by the doctor - she might be able to use that foot massager to advance her healing - but again, I grabbed that because of this company - I was that impressed.

Overall the LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine is a great workout tool and we are happy to have it. I feel like it has added to my workout and will aide me in getting into the shape I’m working towards and my goals.
text_fidelity_b: Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs

Abom 5 in 1 Multicolor Tactical Flashlight Kit, White Red Green Blue Light Torch with Memory Zoomable for Hunting, Fishing, Night Vision, Include Battery, Charger, Traffic Signal Wand Overall, this is a very good flashlight for the price. The build quality is quite good, with an all-metal case, solid tactile feedback on the power button and decent threading. It takes either 3AA (adapter included) or an 18650. While it will work with the AA's, you really need to use an 18650 to get the most out of it. It works well with both flat and button top 18650's. While an adapter is included to prevent battery rattle, the contact springs are strong enough to hold the cell without any rattling. I've tried it with cells from Sanyo, Panasonic, LG and Sony without an issue.

The beam can be focused by sliding the hood. The sliding motion is fairly smooth. Bean strength is excellent considering the price point for this flashlight.

When the flashlight is on, a light press on the power button will cycle it through it's modes (regular, blue, red and green). It's a nice feature to have and sets this apart from other inexpensive single 18650 flashlights. However, it also causes a major irritation -- if you're in regular light mode and turn it off, when you turn it back on it will be in blue mode. You then have to cycle through red and green modes to go back to regular mode. Very annoying -- there should be a separate button (perhaps on the housing) for color, and let the power button be just for power.

That annoyance aside, no complaints. It provides a lot of functionality and value for the price. Four stars overall given the need to cycle through the light modes each time, but otherwise it's a 5-star flashlight for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Abom 5 in 1 Multicolor Tactical Flashlight Kit, White Red Green Blue Light Torch with Memory Zoomable for Hunting, Fishing, Night Vision, Include Battery, Charger, Traffic Signal Wand

text_fidelity_a:
SmooSat SA3(Prime) Electric Scooter for Adults, 20/28 Miles Long Range, 350W Brushless Motor, 8.5/10” Solid Tire, 15.6/20 MPH Max Speed, App Control &Type-C Reverse Charging(Prime Only), LED-Display So my wife loves roller blading and after trying it a number of years back, we discover it is NOT my cup of tea. I miss out when she goes and was trying to think of ways I might still be able to go. I started seeing these eScooters and thought... why not? Had the chance to get one a couple of weeks ago and grabbed it. A short time later I would have the chance to get a second and grabbed it as well, allowing us both to use them when she's not blading.

We like both. Each has a couple "cons," but nothing we can't get over or around. And in the end, we really like them - both. They are each great fun to ride, easy to learn, and have let us enjoy some fun evening rides. Here's our take:

1. Our arrived in the very large box, folded, and needing some assembly before use.

2. There was sadly some damage to the box upon arrival, but didn't notice until - as we worked on the data box - that something seems to have poked a hole through the box, the interior stuffing, the instructions, and finally the end of the handlebars, leaving a gash in the material. It's disappointing, though we do not think caused any damage to how works. We worry about it getting wet in there - as parts to control the bike lie within - but we'll be careful. Though again, disappointing. It's not "brand new perfect."

3. The assembly was mostly easy. Pull up the handle into place, you do have to tighten/loosen/adjust with the included wrench that was truly not worth the cost of making it. One twice and it was slightly bent - but enough it wouldn't grip anymore. Had to use our own adjustable wrench. Got that worked out. Took a few adjustments, but it allows you to lock down the stick holding the handle bars. Once secure the stick and handles bars are very secure throughout the ride. The other eScooter we have allows the handlebars to drop down to fold in and carry in a bag - this does not - and while a nice feature, those also jiggle in a way that makes my wife unfordable while riding. I don't have a problem, but it is a consideration. So this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults makes for a smoother ride for my wife in that regard.

4. Once the stick and handlebars are locked into place, you're pretty much ready to go. It does go down, so you can store it folded, into a smaller piece. The rest of the footprint remains the same - meaning you only loose the height. We have left both open since assembly and find it is easy to get it in and out, but appreciate this feature. The one thing the other eScooter does is to fold down into a smaller overall package - though again, the same footprint size - and fits into an included carrying bag. This SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults does not do that. It is one feature that puts a point into the box for us with the other eScooter and not with this one. If you're working, going to school on a college campus, or maybe out for a ride and want to go in somewhere, being able to pack it into a bag and carry it is a nice feature this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults does not offer - though you can break it down and carry it by hand.

5. The SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults is also noticeably heavier than the other eScooter we got, but for each of us, not so much so we couldn't carry it a distance. You would notice the weight more quickly on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults, but to/from a house, car, or the like it's easy enough.

6. The deck here is pretty decent - size, shape, and traction. My wife feels comfortable on it, but has said a little more room would be nice. But these are eScooters and designed for being useful, but not big. Ironically I'm a bit bigger than her and I am fine - though note the size on both - but ride the smaller other one. Because...

7. With a bit of added weight, I currently do not fit within the posted weight limit of this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults - which is decidedly lower than the other eScooter. Therefore, for safety, I have not even tried this one yet. My wife rides it and does love it. However, the weight difference is interesting in that this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults IS larger and a bit heavier, but the other one comfortably takes my weight in it's posted limits. So it's a bit weird. We feel like this one would likely be fine as well, but won't try. But it also puts another check in the box for the other one.

8. Great bell. Decent light. We both feel like the bell - which sounds similar to a bike bell - is far better on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults, but the light are better on that one. This is doable, but not as large or as bright.

9. There are included tools for assembly, but again, the wrench was worthless after one turn, the others fine. We tossed the wrench, but kept the others if we need to adjust anything.

10. The range on this and the speed are great. I can't tell you off the top of my head what either are listed as, but we've been out and about over a few nights and gone a bit further each time. We're GenX and desk jockeys, so our activity levels had taken a dive - injuries and flu knocked us off our higher actives over the last year or so, though ironically not due to Covid. But getting on these has been a bit of a pacing task. We have been having to adjust to the standing in such a small spot and not moving - no room - so our feet are a bit... they are adjusting. It's been working and each ride we have been more and more comfortable - to the point we no longer stop for our feet being sore. Anyways, the point being, we are both still on the original charge, and we have gone some good distance as we learn and have fun. So we have not charged it yet to know how long. But we are very impressed with the distances we have so far gotten.

11. The speeds are excellent. Again, I've been riding the other one, but my wife easily keeps up. On that one I noticed my current weight does not limit my speed. That one has three speed levels and I'm in the middle. I THINK this one does as well and that she too is using the middle option. Her weight - well within the range of this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults - is no obstacle for her or this eScooter - she can go fast and feel it. We have done some decent "hill" climbing and decent and there is no struggle.

12. The Breaks - WORK! You STOP and you STOP! I mean, hit the breaks and she says it STOPS! The other one has a more reducing speed element - you push the button and it slows you, then you STOP with your feet. In her use of both eScooters, she actually prefers mine - the slowing rather than the STOP. She feels it's far TOO strong and she has to be careful of this so as not to knock herself off. It's not bad - not like she won't use it or is scared of using it - but the reducing speed almost feels like it gives her more control. We have not - yet and hopefully never - had a need to just STOP, but if we did, she's golden.

13. But the reducing speed on the other one allows me to go into controlled corners without stopping, but rather controlling the eScooter. I have a far wider range of speed levels it gives me to do intricate and controlled movements, rather than having to let it "naturally" slow down and do the same on this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults. So two different experiences of control in this way.

In the end, this is a REALLY FUN and well built eScooter. My wife loves it and I look forward to being able to try it when the weight is back down. In the mean time, we can both get out there, go for rides, and have fun. We are thrilled to have it. But... if we had to pick a single eScooter type/make to have, we both agree, we'd likely pick the other one. There is nothing they could have done - again, we feel it was a delivery issue - about the damage to the handlebar. It's disappointing, but we do not hold the eScooter or company responsible.

So that leaves the idea the other one can be broken down and carried in a bag, this one only broken down. This one IS a bit heavier. This one is a bit more of a process to put the handlebars up and down. This one does not have the same weight restrictions as the other - by a long shot of at least 30 lbs difference - meaning larger folks are more limited - check before you buy how much it can hold - so this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults one right away eliminated me from using it until I get these pounds back off. And the STOPPING of this being so abrupt is not our preference.

But in the end, we still truly love this eScooter. It IS a great ride and we have had fun being out. My wife is enjoying it very much. Would we pick the other if we had to? Yes. But for an eScooter, this one is really nice. We cannot - at present - give it anything less than 5 stars for what it does do - meaning we wouldn't drop any stars because of what it doesn't. We're happy to have this SmooSat SA3 Electric Scooter for Adults.
text_fidelity_b: SmooSat SA3(Prime) Electric Scooter for Adults, 20/28 Miles Long Range, 350W Brushless Motor, 8.5/10” Solid Tire, 15.6/20 MPH Max Speed, App Control &Type-C Reverse Charging(Prime Only), LED-Display

Teeter EP-960 Ltd. Inversion Table with Back Pain Relief Kit Really nice piece of equipment. Well constructed and solid. Takes more than the 13-20 minutes setup time that they state. Once you know how to do it you could set it up that quickly, but watching the video and reading the instructions to make sure you are doing it safely and correctly took me about an hour.

I would like someday to try-out the Ironman Gravity 4000 to compare the two. i almost bought the Ironman due to the expense of the Teeter EP-960 Ltd. Also I was a bit concerned that the Ironman vinyl padded cover on the table would make it more difficult for my body to slide down as I was inverting, although it might be more comfortable while just lying flat.

I would definitely recommend this inversion table. I would also caution people to take it slow and gradually increase the angle over a weeks time. My back's muscles took some time to stretch out and get used to moving in ways they had not been. Also it takes time and mental effort to learn to relax completely while being in an inverted angle.

I would give it 5-stars but the price of the unit is high. It was sent second day air by FedEx so that, I am sure, would account for some on the cost.

AC AMERICAN COLLEGIATE Womens Long Sleeves Cotton Hoodie Sweatshirt University & College The search is over and I AM IN LOVE!! For any who’ve been trying for an authentic hoodie- you know, the one made of 100% cotton and not the latest synthetic mixed alternative.. This is it!!
Best of all.. sold at a price point of $30- Are you kidding me!!? Reminiscent of what one would find in a college bookstore..This is a soft, slightly worn in (by appearance only) hoodie that has a timeless and classic look about it. This would stir up memories and make a great gift for any alumni without a doubt.. ha! I actually chose a school that I did not attend- just bc, I loved the hoodie so much!! Plus, I think It’s fair to say the California collegiate system is commercialized in such a way.. making it socially acceptable to wear a name that isn’t affiliated to your education per sé.

For those who don’t know… **These are women’s sizes!! NOTHING unisex about this- IF, wanting men’s/universal sizing- this brand does offer this same item in male standard fit. This is cut and sized for the female figure and in doing so, it eliminates a lot of excess bulk- creating a far more flattering look. Having to order XL to insure a fit thru the bust line.. the chest/mid section fit but, without any room to spare! (Feels more in line with Jr. Miss vs. women’s size?!) The length fits a bit longer due to my height and waistband hits just past the bum cheek. For reference: I’m 5’2”, 154lb, 38C, 40+ yr. old and carry my trouble spot thru the mid/waist section (thx to my x4 kids and gravity!) Hopefully this can give you solid info to compare with.

This is a soft quality mid weight cotton that has been constructed with nice attention to detail.. all seams and stitching are on point..and no loose threads. This can easily be layered up and worn in the colder months or, paired with shorts + flip flops over sunburn shoulders for a summer night.. it’s truly the perfect in-between all season item!

I do recommend washing on cold and line drying.. just to be certain shrinkage won’t alter the fit! (Especially in my situation- where I have no room to spare!) Loving this so much, I’ve worn frequently the past few weeks.. and fingers crossed, I have not had issue with pilling. **double knot hoodie string- or clip together prior to wash- these are prone to disappear into the hoodie in the wash.. trust me, after 2nd time- I got smart!

Hands-down I’d recommend on every level.. this is a great quality, 100% cotton, total classic hoodie that would be appreciated by any- I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Aluminum water bottle cage Is what it is. It's old school, so IMHO it's appropriate on an old-school bike. For contemporary bikes there are MANY better options.

However, for what it is, it is well constructed and handsome.

One star off for the nasty habit of placing logos every-damned-where on bicycle stuff. There is a "Planet Bike" imprint on the most visible part of the cage. If I were putting this on a treasured vintage bike I would feel like that cheapens the build, but as it is I have this on a beloved-but-cheap low end Trek from the late 1980's. I got the bike for $90 on Craigslist and I think this cage is about as low end as I would go on that bike. If I could find one with absolutely no logo for 2x the price I would go for that.
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Aluminum water bottle cage
